text:
Jake Evans is the Canadiens' checking centre, a seventh-round pick from 2014 who has played 438 games for the only NHL team he's known. Martin St-Louis has leaned on him more as the injuries pile up: Florian Xhekaj moved onto his wing when Chris Kreider went down, and Evans has played through a knock of his own that made him a game-time decision against Minnesota.

His results are fair and quietly useful. Eight points in 20 games, with his goals exactly on his expected total, and Montreal takes 55% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, more than 5 points better than without him. On a team whose results are running ahead of its chances, he's one of the forwards actually winning his minutes. His winner against Boston came in a two-point night last week.

He doesn't shoot much, 16 shots on goal all season, and our model compares him to penalty-killing centres like Collin Graf and Marat Khusnutdinov. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking doesn't find a clear strength or weakness, which is about right for a player whose value is not losing. Our talent range has him around 13 goals.
